THE ONLY POINTER HERE THAT CROSSES A REPOSITORY. Everything else in this registry resolves inside one bundle; this one depends on `mac_vocabulary.yaml`, which lives in meaning-as-code and changes on ITS release cycle. A term retired or renamed there breaks every bundle that used it, and nothing in the estate connects the two — you find out when something fails. Measured on contoso5: 13 distinct terms over 101 `mac.*` occurrences, all 13 currently resolving. `eg_build.mac_version` records WHICH framework a verdict was taken against, so a green reading is attributable to a version rather than to "the framework".
AND IT IS THE GAP THAT MADE MIGRATION LOSSY. check_references.py checks these and this registry did not, so retiring the old gate would have dropped ~84 occurrences of the one dependency that spans repositories. With this row the new gate is a superset on every class that has content in this bundle.
`src_kind: '*'` is used HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE, and the reason is the value shape: a key name cannot say what wrote it, but `mac.<ns>.<term>` looks like nothing else, so one row covers every carrier instead of one row per plane.

The inverse of planes_empty_assertion: that one claims a glob matches NOTHING, this one claims it matches SOMETHING. A glob matching nothing is a promise to a consumer that cannot be kept, exactly as a dangling path is.

MEASURED FALSE: contoso5.mac asserts ontology/concepts/**/*.yaml, ontology/rules.yaml and ontology/edges.yaml are all empty. Two of the three are not. A declaration that is actively wrong is worse than a missing one, because a host that trusts it renders nothing and reports no error. `by_glob_empty` is a DELIBERATE seventh resolver, added for this class rather than smuggled in: an assertion of absence cannot be expressed by any of the six.

THIS ROW READ A DEAD ADDRESS FOR SIX DAYS AND MEASURED EMPTY RATHER THAN FAILING, which is the defect the whole catalogue exists against and the second time this one row has carried it. It declared `key_pattern: register` under `src_kind: concept`, i.e. `ontology/concepts/*.yaml -> grounding.sources[].columns.*.rulings.register`. BOTH HALVES OF THAT ADDRESS MOVED: the key was renamed `register` -> `naming`, and the column surface left the concept plane for `ontology/relations/*.yaml#columns.*` when `grounding.sources[]` was retired. `grounding` is now `null` on every contoso5 concept, so the reader resolved nothing.
MEASURED FROM THE COMMITTED GRAPH, not inferred: `vocabulary_group` held 4 objects in every build from 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-07 (commits 1cdd2a6 .. fb9556d) and 0 from 2026-10-08 (c3fc7b8) on, and this kind's references went 5 -> 0 in the same step. The lost objects were `code`, `common`, `legal`, `long` — and those are the exact four terms the relation plane carries today, so nothing about the bundle stopped declaring them. Two sibling rows died in the same move and are recorded on their own rows: `register_pointer_declaration` (5 -> 0) and the whole `register_pointer_*` family, which still read the retired concept surface.
THE ONLY REASON THE LOSS WAS FINDABLE is that the graph is COMMITTED per build, so two builds could be diffed. `registered_unexercised` said 0 nodes and a reader would have taken that for "this bundle does not use naming registers" — the estate's signature failure, a confident empty over an unasked denominator.
CORRECTED 2026-10-02, AND THE EARLIER ERROR IS WORTH KEEPING ON THE RECORD. This row first carried `resolver_arg: ontology/vocabulary.json#register_kind` -- a vocabulary I INVENTED -- and the gate therefore reported five false positives, calling a correctly-authored bundle's most load-bearing key "an undeclared closed vocabulary". The vocabulary exists and always did: mac_vocabulary.yaml#name_register, closed, terms common | legal | long | short | code, and mac_vocabulary.yaml#concept.column.ruling documents the pairing outright -- "`register` says WHICH of that thing's names this one is." All five contoso5 values are valid members. The bundle was right and the reader was wrong, which is the exact failure this whole design is against: a declaration that exists and is not read. It was caught only because a dangling verdict here must carry the BASIS that judged it -- the basis named a file, and the file was wrong. A bare red line would have been believed.

OPERATOR RULING, 2026-10-03: a concept should depend on the register's DECLARATION, not on the data file it describes. Measured at the time: all 51 register bindings pointed at the .csv, so the 17 register descriptors had no inbound declaration at all -- `eg_v_orphan` reported 17 of 17, while SEVEN tools including the runtime resolver read them. Pointing at the declaration makes the chain concept -> register -> csv, turns a .csv rename into one edit instead of 51, and brings `attached` into reach (see register_attached_column — RETIRED 2026-10-15 with `attached[]` itself; the sentence above is the record of 2026-10-03 and the reach it bought is now the reach of THIS row, which is where the pointer lives).
BOTH FORMS ARE REGISTERED ON PURPOSE while the estate migrates: 12 of the bindings are AUTHORED in concepts and can move today; 22 are written by mac_descriptors.py and 17 by mac_lookups.py, so those move when the framework does. A flag day across two repositories is not a migration, it is an outage.

ZERO occurrences in contoso5; the census found the spelling elsewhere in the estate. Declared anyway, because a registry that only lists what one bundle happens to use cannot report that a seventh spelling has appeared. A kind with a population of 0 is a fact, not a gap — and the gate prints it as 0 rather than omitting the row.

Measured: deleting a .csv named by five live pointers of this kind left the referential gate byte-identically green (0/0/0, exit 0), and renaming one was invisible to all 86 gates — because register population is a directory glob (lookups.glob("*.lookup.csv")) rather than a declaration read. A declaration with producers and no consumer gate.

check_dangling_references.py scans 119 md + 0 py docstrings and does not read YAML at all, so it cannot see these. Promoting one of these to register_pointer_path is a one-line edit per concept and is what makes the binding checkable.

THE PROSE MOVED WITH THE BINDING. 7 of contoso5's register references live only inside a sentence -- "NAMES RESOLVE THROUGH `...`" -- and leaving those pointed at the .csv while the machine-readable key moved to the .yaml would have split one fact across two targets, which is the drift this registry exists to find rather than to create.

A COMPOSITE KEY'S PARTS EACH EARN THEIR OWN EDGE, which is the opposite of `check_relation_claims.py`'s own ruling for the UNIQUENESS question it asks ("a composite key is unique AS A TUPLE and never per column... inventing five findings out of nothing"). The two checks are not the same question: that gate asks whether the TUPLE is unique, this one asks what the relation's identity DEPENDS ON — and dropping ANY one part of a composite key breaks the row's own uniqueness claim, so each part is a real, independent dependency edge. `dst_name: canonical` because the target is `<relation>.<column>`, itself dotted — the same reason `concept_grounds_column` and `register_attached_column` (RETIRED 2026-10-15, kept as a comment) carry it.

WITHIN-FILE, like `concept_binds_column`'s own `by_column_in_grounding`: `label_of` names a column of the SAME relation, never a cross-file address, so `by_column_in_relation` never leaves the carrier. A column renamed out from under its own file's `label_of` is the authoring mistake this edge is for -- today unreachable by the pointer catalogue at all, found only by re-profiling the warehouse.

SCOPED BY `src_kind: relation` (home_layer `ontology/relations/`), which is what lets the bare leaf `references` coexist with the two FK rows below: a `relation` file's `references` is always a PascalCase concept id (`value_shape: concept_name`), where a `dataset`/`source` file's is a lowercase `relation.column` string or a `{to: ...}` mapping. The layer check, not the shape, is what keeps the three rows from ever claiming the same node.

A DIFFERENT FIELD NAME FROM THE DATA PLANE'S `register:` on purpose (mac.schema.json#$defs.columnDeclaration vs the TableFile column shape) -- `country_code`'s register binding is declared independently on both `data/datasets/dim_country.yaml` and `ontology/relations/dim_country.yaml`, by design (two authored files annotating one column, the same relationship `relation`'s own column objects have with `dataset`'s).

MEASURED: 12 of 66 declared resource paths do not exist -- 18%. One dataset, one transform, one profile and NINE phantom lookup .csv ids, all left by the dim_date removal of 2026-10-01. This is the manifest a host reads to learn what the bundle IS, so every one of the twelve is a promise to a consumer that cannot be kept, and nothing reports it.

v0.1.19. The step the operator's sequence names — "creation of DECISIONS / decision triggers creation of rules in yaml file" — and it had no pointer, so the link was prose: `why:` is the largest remaining prose block in the worked bundle at 3,501 bytes over 19 rules, mostly sentences of the form "the operator ruled on <date> that ...". CROSS-REPO BY NATURE and that is why `checkers` is empty rather than pretending: a bundle's rule cites a record in `meaning-as-code/decisions/`, which a bundle-scoped gate cannot open, and the estate already counts such targets as UNLOCATED rather than dangling (tools/mac_pointers.py, 346 of them). What CAN be checked, and is owed, is the other direction: a framework-side gate walking every `decided_in` it is handed and resolving it against `decisions/`. Writing `checkers` here before that exists is the hatch verify_enforced_by was built to close. NOT `decided_by`: that spelling is taken, in this very file, for WHO ruled a carve-out (`decided_by: operator`). One name, two meanings, is the defect this catalogue exists to find.
AUDITED 2026-10-15 — FOUR INDEPENDENT REASONS THIS ROW CANNOT FIRE, and it reads as complete. One was fixed; three are OWED and named here so the next reader does not re-derive them.
  1. FIXED. `dst_kind: decision_record` named an object kind this file did not declare, so
     pointer_load's UnstorableReferenceKind guard OMITTED the whole row at load: the NDJSON
     carried 43 reference kinds and the database 42, while the build line printed "43
     kind(s) registered". `decision_record` is now declared in `object_kinds:` and the
     database holds 43 of 43 (measured, scratch build, 2026-10-15). THE CLAIM IS THE
     EQUALITY, NOT THE 43: the catalogue went to 42 rows later the same day when
     `register_attached_column` was retired, and this pair has not been re-measured since.
  2. NOT A BLOCKER — CORRECTED 2026-10-15, after a retirement census held this row to the
     four bundles. This item used to read "`src_kind: rule` cannot be WALKED … the population
     is empty before any key is matched", and that is FALSE: `rule` has no `enumerate` of its
     own, but `_matches` then falls through to the LAYER test, and `home_layer:
     ontology/concepts` admits every concept file. Measured on the four bundles —
     contoso5 17, core 21, tpch 19, exemplars 4 candidate carriers, i.e. the population is
     never empty. And the mutant discriminates in one step: on contoso5's real instance
     (`ontology/concepts/country.yaml` -> `contract.rules[1].decided_in`) change ONLY
     `value_shape` from `repo_qualified_path` to an implemented shape and leave `src_kind:
     rule` alone, and `_matches` goes False -> True. So the file IS in scope and the key DOES
     match; items 3 and 4 are the whole blockage and this one was a wrong diagnosis sitting in
     the authority file. (The original observation it was built on stands and is kept: changing
     `src_kind` ALONE moved nothing — 467 objects / 1011 references / 0 dangling either way.
     The inference that scope was the reason was the error.)
  3. OWED. `resolver: by_repo_path` IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. tools/mac_pointers.py implements 16
     resolvers (by_anchor, by_column_in_descriptor, by_column_in_grounding,
     by_column_in_relation, by_column_in_table, by_concept_name, by_dotted_term,
     by_framework_term, by_glob_empty, by_glob_nonempty, by_id, by_key, by_kind, by_path,
     by_relation_name, by_val) and this is not one of them. A row naming a resolver that does
     not exist measures EMPTY rather than raising, which is the same silence as a dead
     address.
  4. OWED. `value_shape: repo_qualified_path` is outside the CLOSED set the schema declares.
     mac_estate.ddl.sql#eg_reference_kind spells it out: `value_shape TEXT NOT NULL -- CLOSED:
     path | stem | dotted_id | uri | schema_relation | column | kind_token | glob`. Either
     the set widens by declaration or this value is wrong; it may not stay outside it silently.
The bundle DOES carry the instance — ontology/concepts/country.yaml, the rule for which country a sales question means, pointing at meaning-as-code#decisions/RULING-2026-09-30 — and the census counts that key as `observed_unregistered`, i.e. the walk SEES it and no row claims it. So "why does this rule exist" is unanswerable from the graph while a documented row for exactly that question sits here. Items 2-4 are one packet, not three.

THE SAME FACT AS `dataset_column_references`, ON THE RAW PLANE -- a separate row rather than one row naming two `src_kind`s because `_matches`'s layer scoping is keyed to exactly one `src_kind`, and a dedicated pass that collapsed both into one kind name would make this catalogue's own `kind_census` unable to say which PLANE a given dangling FK sat in. CASE IS PRESERVED, never folded: `date.Date` and `date.DATE` are not the same column id on this plane the way `relation_name`'s case-insensitive matching treats a served relation, because the raw columns here are never renamed by a convention this estate controls.

THE CHAIN BROKE AT EVERY SUB-FILE BOUNDARY AND NOTHING SAID SO. `sub_file` gave rules, edges and columns their own objects with a `home_path`, and no EDGE to the file that declares them -- so measured on contoso5 the instant columns arrived: 0 of 24 rules were reachable from their concept and 0 of 60 columns from their dataset. `impact concept/product` had therefore never once reported product's own rules among the things that break, which is the single question this whole graph exists to answer.
DIRECTION: the sub-object DEPENDS ON its file, so dropping the file puts every item it declares in the downstream closure. A column outlives its descriptor in no sense at all.
It is DERIVED, not authored, which is why it is `required: true` with no checker: a missing one is a loader defect, not a bundle defect, and the self-test asserts the count equals the number of sub-file objects.

THE DECLARED TWIN of lineage `feeds`, which is MEASURED. Holding both is what makes a claimed-vs-measured disagreement visible at all — the bundle's own lineage artifact keeps that distinction for the same reason.

THE ONE KIND WITH A WORKING CHECKER, and therefore the model to generalise: of 86 gates, check_transform_sql_extracted was one of only 3 that changed verdict when two .sql files were deleted, and the only one that named both files and the exact key. Registered so the inventory is complete, not because the hole is here. build.sh:57 globs transforms/*.sql, so it cannot notice a deletion -- a deleted transform silently serves fewer relations.
